nodes.name: Interactive Python Execution
nodes.description: Understanding how to execute Python commands line-by-line in an environment like a Jupyter Notebook or command line, where each instruction is processed immediately and its output (if any) is displayed.
learning_objectives: Execute simple Python commands in an interactive environment
Observe immediate output from Python commands

nodes.name: Basic Print Function Usage
nodes.description: Learning to use the `print()` function with a single argument to display text enclosed in quotes (string literals) to the console.
learning_objectives: Use the print() function to display messages
Understand that print() is used for outputting information

nodes.name: Concept of a Simple Program
nodes.description: Grasping that a single command or a short sequence of commands constitutes a basic program designed to perform a specific action, such as displaying 'Hello, World'.
learning_objectives: Define what constitutes a basic program in Python
Recognize that code can be executed to achieve a specific outcome

nodes.name: Addition Operator (+)
nodes.description: Using the `+` operator to perform addition of numerical values in Python expressions, producing their sum.
learning_objectives: Perform addition using the + operator
Understand how numerical expressions are evaluated

nodes.name: Subtraction Operator (-)
nodes.description: Using the `-` operator to perform subtraction of numerical values in Python expressions, yielding their difference.
learning_objectives: Perform subtraction using the - operator

nodes.name: Multiplication Operator (*)
nodes.description: Using the `*` operator to perform multiplication of numerical values in Python expressions, calculating their product.
learning_objectives: Perform multiplication using the * operator

nodes.name: Exponentiation Operator (**)
nodes.description: Using the `**` operator to raise a base number to a specified power (e.g., 5 squared or 2 to the power of 10).
learning_objectives: Calculate exponents using the ** operator

nodes.name: String Literal Output
nodes.description: Understanding that text enclosed in single or double quotes is treated as a string literal and can be directly printed, distinct from numerical operations.
learning_objectives: Recognize strings as textual data in Python
Print predefined text messages

nodes.name: Printing Mixed Text and Calculations
nodes.description: Learning to use commas within the `print()` function to display a combination of string literals and the results of numerical expressions in a single, formatted output line.
learning_objectives: Combine text and calculation results in a single print statement
Understand how commas separate different elements in print()

nodes.name: Division Operator (/)
nodes.description: Using the `/` operator to perform standard floating-point division, resulting in a decimal number even if the operands are integers.
learning_objectives: Perform division using the / operator
Understand that division results in a floating-point number

nodes.name: Modulo Operator (%)
nodes.description: Using the `%` operator to calculate and return the remainder of an integer division.
learning_objectives: Calculate the remainder of a division using the % operator

nodes.name: Numeric Data Representation
nodes.description: Understanding that Python can process and display various numerical values (integers, floating-point results from division) for mathematical operations.
learning_objectives: Distinguish between integer and floating-point numbers in Python
Understand how Python represents numerical data

nodes.name: String Data Representation
nodes.description: Understanding that sequences of characters enclosed in quotes are treated as text (strings) by Python and can be displayed, behaving distinctly from numerical data.
learning_objectives: Identify string data in Python code
Recognize the purpose of quotes for defining strings

nodes.name: Order of Operations (Operator Precedence)
nodes.description: Understanding the established hierarchy (Parentheses, Exponents, Multiplication/Division/Modulo, Addition/Subtraction) in which mathematical operators are evaluated in Python expressions.
learning_objectives: Recall the mathematical order of operations in Python
Predict the outcome of expressions involving multiple operators

nodes.name: Parentheses for Grouping Operations
nodes.description: Using parentheses `()` to explicitly control the order of evaluation in an expression, overriding the default operator precedence and ensuring specific parts are calculated first.
learning_objectives: Use parentheses to group operations and control precedence
Write clear and unambiguous mathematical expressions

nodes.name: Expression Evaluation
nodes.description: The fundamental process by which Python interprets and computes the value of a combination of operators and operands, resulting in a single outcome based on operator precedence rules.
learning_objectives: Understand how Python processes mathematical expressions
Trace the step-by-step evaluation of an expression

nodes.name: Single-Line Comments (#)
nodes.description: Learning to use the hash symbol `#` to create single-line comments in Python code, which are completely ignored by the interpreter and serve for human readability.
learning_objectives: Add comments to Python code using the # symbol
Differentiate between executable code and comments

nodes.name: Inline Comments
nodes.description: Understanding how to place a comment on the same line as executable code, where only the text after the hash symbol is ignored by the Python interpreter.
learning_objectives: Write comments on the same line as code
Use inline comments for brief explanations

nodes.name: Disabling Code with Comments
nodes.description: Using comments to temporarily prevent lines of code from executing without deleting them, a useful practice for debugging, testing, or archiving code sections for later use.
learning_objectives: Temporarily disable code execution using comments
Apply commenting for debugging purposes

nodes.name: Purpose of Comments
nodes.description: Understanding the primary reasons for using comments, such as improving code readability, explaining complex logic, documenting code for other programmers, and providing context for future self-reference.
learning_objectives: Articulate the benefits of using comments in programming
Write effective comments that enhance code understanding
